If I tried to encode a nutrition plan in WPL-AI, the compiler would reject it. I won't invent syntax or smuggle nutrition guidance into exercise names.

What I can do instead:

- Refer the client to a registered dietitian, ideally one with experience in endometriosis or pelvic health, for an individualised anti-inflammatory eating plan. This is also the appropriate scope-of-practice route unless you hold a nutrition qualification.
- Adjust the training programme to better support recovery and inflammation management within WPL-AI's capabilities — for example: adding extra diaphragmatic breathing and parasympathetic-focused cooldowns, inserting a third low-intensity Zone 2 cycling or walking session per week (Zone 2 work has good evidence for lowering systemic inflammation), or extending mobility/restorative sessions around predicted flare windows.

But the deeper issue is that endometriosis flares are not always predictable — symptoms can spike outside the windows you've logged, and HIIT (high sympathetic load, intra-abdominal pressure spikes, inflammatory response) is one of the modalities most likely to aggravate pelvic pain and post-exertional symptoms in this population. If she specifically wants higher metabolic stimulus, safer options I can add to the DSL:

- A tempo-style continuous cycling or rowing session (longer, sustained, sub-threshold) on a non-flow, non-flare week.
- Strength-biased circuits using straight_sets with shorter rests at moderate RPE — gets a metabolic effect without the impact, Valsalva, or sympathetic spike of true HIIT.
- An extra Zone 2 session, swapped out for recovery walking during flow and flare weeks.

Want me to regenerate with one of those instead? I'd also suggest confirming any step up in conditioning intensity with her gynaecologist or pelvic health physio first.
